Ethan Rivera: FYI — customer hit a hard failure on embeddings after yesterday's deploy. their app logs: 'AssertionError: embedding length mismatch (expected 1536, got 1024)'. they say nothing changed client-side.

Priya Nair: can you grab the sample request and which model(s) they were using? also SDK/lang/versions.

Ethan Rivera: pasted sanitized request from them:
```json
{
  \"model\": \"rw-embed-l\",
  \"inputs\": [\"alpha\", \"beta\"],
  \"batch\": true
}
```
They also have other workers calling `rw-embed-s`. App uses node sdk 0.11.2.

Jules (oncall): this reads like mixed-model batching. our coalescing layer groups by batching key; if the key doesn't include model variant or vector-dim, two workers can end up in same physical batch. kernel then throws.

Ramya S.: quick check: do we still rely on client to set X-Redwood-Model header? newer SDKs add a per-request model tag that the router uses. older ones don't. 0.11.2 might be in the window.

Priya Nair: customer error was noisy (stack traces). we should give them a clearer HTTP error and also a short support runbook.

Jules (oncall): agreed. action plan: (1) runtime: add pre-batch validation for consistent embedding size across requests assembled into a single batch -> return 400 with friendly message. I'll cut a small patch to canary today. (2) router: update batching key to include model + quant/profile to avoid mixing in future. (3) docs and CS playbook update. I'll file an incident.

support-bot: INC-2521 opened: \"embeddings batching mixed models -> dimension errors\" assigned to eng-runtime.

Ethan Rivera: customer repro notes: 8 node workers behind a load balancer, feature flag toggles model per request (rw-embed-l vs rw-embed-s). They do `client.embeddings({model, input: texts})` with implicit client batching (batch size ~16). When both variants are hot they sometimes see the failure.

Luca Chen: on docs — we mention batching but not this specific failure mode. I'll add an FAQ entry & short runbook for CS with sample repro and mitigation steps. Suggested temporary fixes for customers: pin model per process, disable client auto-batching, or upgrade SDK to >=0.12.0 which includes batching headers.

Ramya S.: one more nuance — if customers use different quantization profiles of the same model (e.g., rw-embed-l and rw-embed-l-8bit) mismatch can still happen; we should mention that explicitly.

Priya Nair: suggested customer reply draft: 
"Hey — sorry for the disruption. The error you're seeing occurs when requests for different embedding models (or different quantization profiles) are combined into one backend batch. Short-term options: 1) ensure each worker/process only calls one model variant; 2) set `client.disableAutoBatching = true` in your SDK config; 3) upgrade to our Node SDK >=0.12.0. We're pushing a runtime fix to surface a clearer error and updating our docs. Ticket INC-2521 created."

Ethan Rivera: sending that now and asking for a small reproducible script.

Jules (oncall): runtime error format we'll return in canary: `HTTP 400 { \"error\": \"embedding size mismatch: batch contains vectors of lengths [1024,1536]\" }`. Also logging will include the model ids seen in the batch for debugging.

Luca Chen: runbook snippet I'll PR (#1002):
```
Q: Why did my embeddings call fail with a dimension mismatch?
A: This happens when multiple requests in a single backend batch target different embedding outputs (different models or quantization profiles).
Mitigations:
- Pin model per process or per container (recommended).
- Disable automatic batching while migrating: `client.disableAutoBatching = true`.
- Upgrade to SDK >=0.12.0 so the router receives per-request model metadata.
- If mixing is required, send separate API calls per model type (do not let client coalesce them).
Support runbook for CS:
1) Ask for SDK language & version, exact `model` strings used, and a small repro.
2) Check server logs for mixed-model IDs within the same batching window.
3) Recommend mitigations above; if the customer can't move immediately, enable canary with patched runtime that returns clear 400s so they can identify offending requests.
4) Escalate to eng-runtime (INC-2521) if logs show model mixing despite SDK headers set.
```

support-bot: INC-2521 updated: runtime canary patched; docs PR #1002 opened.

Priya Nair: owners: Jules -> runtime patch + router key change, Luca -> docs & FAQ PR, Ethan/Ramya -> customer liaison. ETA: customer note out in 1 hour, canary error by EOD, router key fix next sprint.

Ethan Rivera: thanks — I'll keep this thread updated after customer tries the short-term mitigations. :thumbsup:
